target_customer: Families of children with cerebral palsy and other mobility disabilities (lease or purchase, often via insurance funding), plus hospitals and clinics
problem: Children with cerebral palsy and similar conditions have few options to walk upright; most exoskeletons were built for adults and were bulky and costly.
business_model: Hardware lease and sale of pediatric exoskeletons (consumer lease of $899 per month at launch) with clinic and home use

founders.name: Manmeet Maggu
education: University of Waterloo, BASc 2013, mechanical and mechatronics engineering
founders.background_notes: Started the device as a fourth year design project inspired by his nephew with cerebral palsy. Sources: YC page, University of Waterloo engineering news.

founders.name: Rahul Udasi
education: University of Waterloo, BASc 2014, mechanical and mechatronics engineering
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page and called co-founder by TechCrunch 2019-02-25.

technical_complexity.rationale: A wearable gait exoskeleton for growing children needs custom mechatronics, safety design and clinical validation; the team iterated through about six device versions and ran a clinical study at Cincinnati Children's Hospital by 2019.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware, clinical evidence and later FDA 510(k) clearance raise the bar, though the first product was marketed as an exercise product to avoid some FDA requirements.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the pediatric niche in sources found; the company reached over 450 units in 40 countries by mid 2025.

market_need_then: TechCrunch 2019-02-25 reported the founders found nothing on the market for a child needing to walk outside therapy; the UW article says most exoskeletons were designed for adults.

branding.domain_note: Uses trexorobotics.com (name plus descriptor); no acquisition history found.

identity.visual_style: Device rings light up in white, blue, purple and pink to show status
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, family centered and careful about medical claims; 'Because for a child, walking is more than getting around.'

branding.brand_signature: The 'robotic legs' framing and the 100 million steps milestone
branding.community_and_virality: Press release milestones (100 million steps, Dec 2024) and family funding appeal stories show a community of families; no merch or fan accounts found.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong founder story and steady milestone press in medical and robotics outlets, but a niche medical brand with limited consumer reach.

outcome_analysis: Trexo grew from a family driven design project into a pediatric exoskeleton maker with 450 or more units in 40 countries by mid 2025 and an FDA 510(k) clearance for its newer device. Founder market fit and clinical work helped, but reported funding is small and unverified, and new shipments are now dated 2027, so capital intensity and reimbursement look like the main constraints.
notes: Funding seen only in aggregators and unverified: CB Insights $720K over 6 rounds (incl. 2019 convertible note, 2024 accelerator round), Seedtable seed entries, a Spanish database showing $150K convertible at $2.0M and EUR 227K total. None cross-checked, so no rounds recorded. Competitors: searches found no 2018 to 2019 dated sources naming pediatric rivals (Marsi Bionics source undated), so list is empty. Outcome search found no shutdown, acquisition or recall; a Dec 2025 job post and 2026 CB Insights news item suggest ongoing operations.
